resolutions.researcher_notes: No source explicitly corroborates GEM Status 'shelved'. MEED (24 May 2011) shows the project only ever reached the EPC bidding stage: South Oil Company tendered it in April 2011, 20+ firms submitted bids, construction was expected to take 10 months — no evidence it advanced. The Arabic ahewar survey (30 May 2022) still lists it as a planned/target project, not as shelved. So 'shelved' is a reasonable GEM inference from a stalled 2011 tender that never progressed, but it is NOT directly stated by any independent source, and the 2022 source mildly contradicts it by treating the line as still planned. Leaving proposed_refs empty to avoid an unsupported ref; flagging the disagreement for human review.

Original current_ref (bncnetwork) is dead (verifier: 200 but content missing). Replaced with two independent sources that both state the 100 MMcf/d capacity. MEED (2011, English): 18-inch pipeline 'to carry up to 100 million cubic feet a day (cf/d) of gas'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'بطاقة 100 مليون قدم مكعب في اليوم' (capacity 100 million cubic feet per day). Two independent publications, different years/languages -> high.

Original current_ref (bncnetwork) dead; replaced. MEED (2011): '105-kilometre-long gas pipeline connecting the Zubair oil field to the Fao oil depot ... the Fao depot 105km away'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'بطول 105 كيلومتر' (length 105 km). Two independent sources agree on 105 km -> high.

Original current_ref (bncnetwork) dead; replaced. MEED (2011): '18-inch carbon steel gas pipeline'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'وقطر 18 بوصة' (diameter 18 inches). Two independent sources agree on 18 in -> high.

FuelSource = Zubair (gas sourced from the Zubair field). MEED (2011): gas carried 'from a depot at the Zubair field near Basra'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'خط أنابيب من حقل الزبير' (pipeline from the Zubair field). Both name Zubair as the source field -> high.

Route corroborated: starts at Zubair field near Basra (StartState/Province Basrah, Iraq) and ends at the Fao/Al-Faw depot on Iraq's Gulf coast (EndLocation Al Faw, Al-Faw Peninsula, Iraq). MEED (2011): 'from a depot at the Zubair field near Basra to the Fao depot 105km away ... the Fao oil depot on Iraq's Gulf coast'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'من حقل الزبير إلى الفاو' (from Zubair field to Fao). Two independent sources agree -> high.

GEM Owner1 = Iraq Ministry of Oil (100%). MEED (2011) reports the project was tendered by state-owned South Oil Company (SOC), 'a state-owned regional upstream operator'. SOC is a subsidiary/regional operating company of the Iraq Ministry of Oil, so this corroborates state/Ministry-of-Oil ownership. Only one source directly names the state owner (ahewar does not clearly attribute ownership) -> medium. Nuance to flag: MEED names South Oil Company specifically as the tendering/operating entity, whereas GEM records the parent 'Iraq Ministry of Oil'.
